responsibility: This is the main implementation file of the AVR GCC backend, tying the target into GCC’s middle end, RTL expansion, reload, costing, assembly output, calling convention, and AVR-specific memory model. It owns the concrete logic behind most `targetm` hooks for register usage, argument passing, return values, prologue/epilogue generation, section and symbol encoding, address-space support for flash and MEMX, builtin declaration/expansion/folding, operand printing, machine-dependent reorganization, and cost modeling, while also maintaining AVR-specific data such as address-space descriptors, special-function-register addresses, and helpers used by the machine-description patterns in `avr.md` and companion files.
same_name_distinction: This is the executable implementation companion to the other same-stem AVR files: unlike avr.h it defines the target hooks, helper routines, and backend data bodies (such as address-space tables) rather than declarations/macros; unlike avr.md it is imperative C code that those RTL patterns and generated insn files rely on for costs, printing, reorg, builtins, and prologue/epilogue logic; and unlike avr.opt it consumes the AVR option variables instead of declaring the option table itself.
